en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
Ārāmavagga 53.
The Training Rule on Rebuking a Group.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the nun Caṇḍakāḷī was one who caused quarrels, who caused strife, who caused disputes, who caused contention, and who caused legal issues in the Saṅgha.
While a formal act was being performed against her, the nun Thullanandā protested.
At that time, the nun Thullanandā had gone to a village on some business.
Then the community of bhikkhunīs, thinking,
"The bhikkhunī Thullanandā has departed," suspended the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī for not seeing her offense.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having finished that business in the village, returned once again to Sāvatthī.
When the bhikkhunī Thullanandā was approaching, the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī neither prepared a seat for her, nor set out water for washing the feet, a footstool, or a foot-wiping cloth;
she did not go out to meet her to receive her bowl and robe, nor did she offer her water.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to the bhikkhunī Caṇḍakāḷī:
“Noble lady, why is it that when I was coming, you neither prepared a seat nor set out water for washing the feet, a footstool, and a foot-wiping cloth;
nor did you go out to meet me to receive my bowl and robe, nor offer me water to drink?
“It is indeed so, noble lady, as it would be for one who is without a protector.”
“But why, noble lady, are you without a protector?
“Noble lady, these bhikkhunīs have suspended me for not seeing an offense, saying: ‘This woman is without a protector and unknown; she has no one at all to oppose her.’”

The bhikkhunī Thullanandā, thinking, “These women are foolish, incompetent, and ignorant; they do not know what is a formal act, a defect in a formal act, a failure of a formal act, or a success of a formal act,” being fierce, reviled the Saṅgha.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as before]... were indignant, complained, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā, having become fierce, revile the community? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, monks, that the nun Thullanandā, having become fierce, reviles the community?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How indeed, bhikkhus, can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā, having become fierce, revile a group?
This, bhikkhus, is neither for the inspiration of those without confidence nor for the increase of those with confidence…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule as follows:
“Whatever nun, being angry, should revile a group, that is an offense entailing expiation (pācittiya).
Whatever nun means:
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... [pe] ...a nun...
[pe] ...this is the nun intended in this context.
"Caṇḍīkatā" means one who is prone to anger.
"Gaṇa" means...
“The community of bhikkhunīs” is what is meant.
“Should revile” means:

she reviles them, saying, “These women are fools, these women are incompetent; they do not know the formal act, nor the defect in a formal act, nor the failure of a formal act, nor the success of a formal act”; there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If she reviles several bhikkhunīs, or a single bhikkhunī, or one who is not fully ordained, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if she does so with a motive of benefit.
one who prioritizes the Dhamma,
one who prioritizes instruction,
and one who is insane.
"Regarding the first offender":
thus ends the third training rule.
